examples.en: A pretty dress is hanging in the shop window.

examples.ko: 지나가다가 쇼윈도 속 구두가 마음에 들었어요.
examples.en: While passing by, I liked the shoes in the shop window.
The shop owner decorated the window display anew.

examples.ko: 쇼윈도 앞에서 아이가 한참 서 있어요.
examples.en: The child has been standing in front of the shop window for a while.
The shop window lights stay on even at night.
I saw the sale notice stuck on the shop window.

explain: '진열대'는 가게 안에도 있지만, 쇼윈도는 밖에서 유리 너머로 구경하는 곳이에요. 보통 '쇼윈도를 구경하다', '쇼윈도에 진열하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 저 부부는 남들 앞에서만 다정한 쇼윈도 부부래요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사이가 좋지 않은데 남들에게는 사이좋은 척하는 부부를 말해요. 조금 비꼬는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A couple who act happy in public but are not close in private. It sounds a bit sarcastic.
phrases.en_equiv: a couple putting on a show for others

explain_en: A '진열대' (display shelf) can be inside a shop, but a 쇼윈도 is the glass display you look at from outside. It is usually used as '쇼윈도를 구경하다' (to window-shop) or '쇼윈도에 진열하다' (to display in the window).

examples.ko: 이 학원은 합격하면 수강료 전액을 돌려준다고 광고했어요.
examples.en: This academy advertised that it would refund the full tuition if you pass.
How much is the tuition per month?

examples.ko: 수강료를 카드로 나눠서 낼 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can I pay the tuition by card in installments?
The tuition is so expensive that I am torn.
If you register early, they take 10 percent off the tuition.
You need the tuition receipt to get a refund.

explain: 학원이나 강좌 이름 뒤에 붙는 돈은 '학원비'라고도 해요. 대학교에서 내는 돈은 '수강료'가 아니라 보통 '등록금'이라고 해요.
explain_en: For private academies people also say '학원비'. The money paid to a university is usually called '등록금', not 수강료.

examples.en: I put up a towel rack on the bathroom wall.
The towel rack fell off, so I have to put it back.

examples.ko: 수건걸이에 걸린 수건이 아직 젖어 있어요.
examples.en: The towel hanging on the rack is still wet.

examples.ko: 새 집에 맞는 수건걸이를 사러 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to buy a towel rack that fits the new house.

examples.ko: 수건걸이 위치가 너무 높은 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think the towel rack is too high.
Using a hook instead of a towel rack is fine too.

explain: '옷걸이', '열쇠걸이'처럼 '-걸이'는 무언가를 걸어 두는 물건 이름에 붙어요. '수건 걸이'로 띄지 않고 한 단어로 붙여 써요.
explain_en: Like '옷걸이' (clothes hanger) and '열쇠걸이' (key rack), '-걸이' attaches to names of things used for hanging items. Write it as one word, not '수건 걸이'.

examples.en: My brother is quiet, but I am a chatterbox.
My friend is an incurable chatterbox.

examples.ko: 수다쟁이 동생 덕분에 집이 늘 시끌시끌해요.
examples.en: Thanks to my chatty younger sibling, the house is always noisy.

examples.ko: 우리 반 수다쟁이가 오늘은 웬일로 조용해요.
examples.en: For some reason, the chatterbox of our class is quiet today.

examples.ko: 수다쟁이 할머니가 이웃 이야기를 다 알고 계세요.
examples.en: The chatty grandmother knows all the stories about the neighbors.

examples.ko: 저는 원래 수다쟁이가 아닌데 그 사람 앞에서는 말이 많아져요.
examples.en: I am not normally a chatterbox, but I talk a lot in front of that person.

explain: '멋쟁이', '고집쟁이'처럼 '-쟁이'가 붙은 말이라 친근하거나 놀리는 느낌이 있어요. 윗사람에게 직접 쓰면 실례일 수 있어요. 성격을 부드럽게 말할 때는 '말이 많다', '수다스럽다'를 써요.
explain_en: Like '멋쟁이' and '고집쟁이', the '-쟁이' ending gives it a friendly or teasing tone. It can be rude to use directly about someone older. For a softer description, say '말이 많다' or '수다스럽다'.

examples.en: The patient is lying quietly on the operating table.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 수술대 앞에서 손을 씻어요.
examples.en: The doctor washes his hands in front of the operating table.

examples.ko: 수술대 위에는 불이 아주 환하게 켜져 있어요.
examples.en: A very bright light is on above the operating table.
I saw a scene in a drama where someone goes onto the operating table.

examples.ko: 아버지가 내일 수술대에 오르셔서 너무 떨려요.
examples.en: My father goes in for surgery tomorrow, so I am very nervous.
The operating table looks narrower and colder than I expected.

explain: '수술대에 오르다'는 수술을 받으러 들어간다는 말인데, 조금 긴장된 느낌이 있어요. 일상에서 그냥 말할 때는 '수술을 받다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 오래된 입시 제도가 드디어 수술대에 올랐어요.
phrases.en: be put on the operating table
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 있는 제도나 조직이 크게 고쳐질 대상이 된다는 뜻이에요. 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: A flawed system or organization becomes a target for major reform. Often seen in the news.

explain_en: '수술대에 오르다' means going in for surgery and carries a slightly tense feeling. In ordinary conversation, '수술을 받다' (to have surgery) sounds more natural.

examples.en: Our country imports oil, so it is sensitive to fuel prices.

examples.ko: 한국은 이 과일의 주요 수입국 중 하나예요.
examples.en: Korea is one of the main importing countries of this fruit.
With more importing countries involved, the price went down a little.
It is safer if you increase the variety of importing countries.
I saw on the news which countries import rice.
The importing country raised taxes, so the price of the goods went up.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '수출국'이에요. 뉴스에서는 '주요 수입국', '최대 수입국'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '수출국' (exporting country). In the news it appears as '주요 수입국' (main importing country) or '최대 수입국' (largest importing country).

examples.ko: 수저통에서 숟가락 두 개만 꺼내 주세요.
examples.en: Please take just two spoons out of the utensil holder.
There is a utensil holder on every table in the restaurant.
The utensil holder is empty, so please fill it quickly.
I washed the utensil holder clean and left it to dry.

examples.ko: 이사 가서 새 수저통을 하나 샀어요.
examples.en: After moving, I bought a new utensil holder.
The child spilled the chopsticks from the utensil holder.

explain: '수저'는 숟가락과 젓가락을 함께 부르는 말이라 수저통에는 둘 다 들어가요. 식당에서 수저를 직접 꺼내 쓰게 놓아 둔 통도 이렇게 불러요.
explain_en: '수저' refers to a spoon and chopsticks together, so both go into a 수저통. At restaurants, the container left on the table for self-service utensils is also called this.

examples.en: On rainy days, I think of sujebi.
You tear off thin pieces of dough and put them in.

examples.ko: 어머니가 끓여 주신 수제비가 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: The sujebi my mother made is the most delicious.
For lunch, I ate sujebi instead of kalguksu.

examples.ko: 수제비에 감자랑 애호박을 넣으면 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: It tastes better if you add potato and zucchini to the sujebi.
Please give me one more bowl of sujebi.

explain: 칼국수와 비슷해 보이지만, 수제비는 반죽을 칼로 썰지 않고 손으로 떼어 넣어요. 그래서 모양이 조금씩 달라요.
explain_en: It looks similar to kalguksu, but sujebi dough is torn by hand instead of cut with a knife. That is why each piece has a slightly different shape.

examples.en: My younger sibling gets shy in front of strangers.
The child could not even say hello and was shy.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 칭찬을 받으면 수줍어하며 웃어요.
examples.en: That friend smiles shyly when praised.
Why are you so shy? Please speak freely.

examples.ko: 처음 만난 자리라서 다들 조금 수줍어했어요.
examples.en: It was a first meeting, so everyone was a little shy.

examples.ko: 수줍어하지 말고 앞에 나와서 노래해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't be shy, come to the front and sing.

explain: '수줍다'는 형용사이고, '수줍어하다'는 다른 사람이 수줍어하는 모습을 보고 말할 때 자주 써요. '부끄러워하다'는 잘못해서도 쓰지만, 수줍어하다는 낯을 가리거나 쑥스러운 느낌이에요.
explain_en: '수줍다' is an adjective, while '수줍어하다' is often used when you describe someone's shy behavior. '부끄러워하다' can also be used for shame over a mistake, but 수줍어하다 means feeling bashful or self-conscious around others.

examples.en: This painting sold for tens of millions of won.
Tens of millions of people listened to this song.
Dinosaurs lived tens of millions of years ago.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 수천만 달러를 벌었다고 해요.
examples.en: They say that movie earned tens of millions of dollars.

examples.ko: 집을 사려면 수천만 원이 더 필요해요.
examples.en: To buy a house, I need tens of millions of won more.

examples.ko: 수천만 개의 별이 하늘에 떠 있어요.
examples.en: Tens of millions of stars are floating in the sky.

explain: 한국어는 만 단위로 세기 때문에 '수천만'은 천만 단위가 몇 번 들어간 큰 수예요. '수천 만'처럼 띄지 않고 붙여 쓰고, 보통 '수천만 원', '수천만 명'처럼 단위 앞에 와요. '몇천만'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: Korean counts in units of 만 (10,000), so 수천만 is a big number made of several thousands of 만, i.e. tens of millions. Write it together, not as '수천 만', and it usually comes before a unit, as in '수천만 원' or '수천만 명'. You can also say '몇천만'.

examples.en: Thousands upon thousands of people gathered in the square.
Countless stars twinkle in the night sky.

examples.ko: 수천수만 가지 이유가 있겠지만 저는 이게 제일 중요해요.
examples.en: There may be countless reasons, but I think this one is the most important.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 노래는 수천수만 번 들어도 안 질려요.
examples.en: I never get tired of that singer's songs, even after listening thousands of times.
Thousands upon thousands of birds took off all at once.
Countless flowers bloomed all at once.

explain: 정확한 숫자가 아니라 '아주 많다'를 강조하는 말이에요. 보통 '수천수만 명', '수천수만 개', '수천수만 가지'처럼 뒤에 단위가 와요. 비슷한 '수많은'은 더 평범하고 일상적이에요.
explain_en: It is not an exact number but an emphasis on 'a huge amount'. A unit usually follows, as in '수천수만 명', '수천수만 개', '수천수만 가지'. The similar '수많은' sounds plainer and more everyday.

examples.en: I went to have sundaetguk for lunch with a friend.
I add a little salted shrimp to my sundaetguk.
How much is a bowl of sundaetguk here?
On cold days, I crave hot sundaetguk.
I put rice in the sundaetguk and ate it.

examples.ko: 이 집 순댓국은 국물이 진하고 구수해요.
examples.en: This place's sundaetguk has a rich, savory broth.

explain: 소리 내서는 [순대꾹]이라 말하지만 사이시옷 때문에 '순댓국'이라고 써요. 보통 새우젓이나 깍두기를 곁들여 먹어요.
explain_en: It is pronounced [순대꾹] but spelled with the sai-siot, as '순댓국'. It is usually eaten with salted shrimp or kkakdugi (radish kimchi).

examples.en: This place's soft tofu stew is a little spicy.
I add an egg to the soft tofu stew and eat it.
Soft tofu is gentle and easy to eat.
I bought soft tofu and made a stew.

examples.ko: 간장을 살짝 넣어서 순두부를 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: It tastes good to eat soft tofu with a little soy sauce.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 순두부가 아주 부드럽고 고소해요.
examples.en: The soft tofu at this restaurant is very smooth and nutty.

explain: 보통 두부는 눌러서 굳히지만, 순두부는 굳히기 전이라 몽글몽글하고 부드러워요. 그래서 찌개로 많이 끓여 먹어요.
explain_en: Regular tofu is pressed to firm up, but 순두부 is not yet pressed, so it is soft and curdy. That is why it is often cooked into stew.

examples.en: Who is it this round?
I lost at rock-paper-scissors, so I became the seeker.
The seeker closes their eyes and counts to ten.
Hide quickly so the seeker doesn't catch you!
My younger sibling grumbles that they don't want to be it all the time.
We played rock-paper-scissors to decide who would be it.

explain: '술래가 되다', '술래를 정하다'처럼 써요. 숨바꼭질에서는 찾는 사람이고, 얼음땡 같은 놀이에서는 쫓아가는 사람이에요.
explain_en: It is used as '술래가 되다' (to be it) or '술래를 정하다' (to choose who is it). In hide-and-seek it is the one who searches, and in games like freeze tag it is the chaser.

examples.en: The children are happily playing tag in the park.
I fell while playing tag and hurt my knee.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 동네 친구들과 술래잡기를 자주 했어요.
examples.en: As a child, I often played tag with the neighborhood kids.

examples.ko: 오늘은 술래잡기 말고 다른 놀이를 해요.
examples.en: Let's play a different game today instead of tag.

examples.ko: 술래잡기에서는 잡힌 사람이 다음 술래가 돼요.
examples.en: In tag, the person who gets caught becomes the next "it."
Shall we all play tag together?

explain: 원래는 술래가 숨은 사람을 찾는 놀이라서 '숨바꼭질'과 같은 말이에요. 요즘은 술래가 쫓아가서 잡는 놀이도 술래잡기라고 해요. '술래잡기하다'처럼 동사로도 써요.
explain_en: Originally it is the game where the seeker looks for hidden people, so it means the same as '숨바꼭질'. These days it also refers to a game where the chaser runs after and catches others. It also works as a verb, as in '술래잡기하다'.

examples.en: My child is totally hooked on hidden picture games.
I found five cats in the hidden picture puzzle.
There is a hidden picture puzzle on the back page of the book.
You need good eyes to be good at hidden picture games.

examples.ko: 동생과 누가 먼저 찾나 숨은그림찾기를 했어요.
examples.en: My sibling and I did a hidden picture puzzle to see who would find it first.
This hidden picture puzzle was so hard that I gave up.

explain: '숨은 그림'이 아니라 '숨은그림찾기'를 한 단어로 붙여 써요. '숨은그림찾기를 하다', '숨은그림찾기를 풀다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is written as one word, '숨은그림찾기', not '숨은 그림 찾기'. People say '숨은그림찾기를 하다' or '숨은그림찾기를 풀다'.

examples.ko: 신문을 배달하려고 매일 숲길을 걸어야 했어요.
examples.en: To deliver newspapers, I had to walk along the forest path every day.
The air felt cool when we entered the persimmon grove path.
Every weekend I take a walk on the forest trail with my family.
It rained earlier, so the forest path is slippery.
There is a small cafe at the end of the forest path.

examples.ko: 이 숲길은 가을에 단풍이 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: This forest path has really beautiful autumn leaves in the fall.

explain: 산에 난 길은 '산길', 나무가 많은 길은 '숲길'이라고 해요. 보통 '숲길을 걷다', '숲길을 산책하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: A path on a mountain is a '산길', while a path among many trees is a '숲길'. It is usually used as '숲길을 걷다' or '숲길을 산책하다'.

examples.en: I bought a file and a stapler at the stationery store.
The staples have already run out.
Staple the documents and submit them.

examples.ko: 스테이플러 좀 빌려 줄 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you lend me a stapler?

examples.ko: 스테이플러가 고장 났는지 종이가 안 찍혀요.
examples.en: The stapler seems broken, because it won't staple the paper.
Where did you put the stapler that was on the desk?

explain: 종이를 찍는 것은 '찍다'를 써서 '스테이플러로 찍다'라고 해요. 한국에서는 '호치키스'라고 부르는 사람도 많아요.
explain_en: You use the verb '찍다' for stapling, as in '스테이플러로 찍다'. Many people in Korea also call it '호치키스'.

examples.en: What is the spelling of this word?
The spelling was wrong, so I couldn't find it in the dictionary.

examples.ko: 제 이름 스펠링을 천천히 불러 드릴게요.
examples.en: I'll read out the spelling of my name slowly.
English spelling is hard to memorize.

examples.ko: 스펠링 하나만 틀려도 메일이 안 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even one wrong letter can keep the email from being delivered.

examples.ko: 메일 주소 스펠링을 다시 확인해 주세요.
examples.en: Please check the spelling of the email address again.

explain: '철자'와 같은 뜻인데, 말할 때는 '스펠링'이 더 편하게 들려요. 한국어 글자의 규칙은 '맞춤법'이라고 해서 따로 불러요.
explain_en: It means the same as '철자', but '스펠링' sounds more casual in speech. The rules for writing Korean correctly are called '맞춤법', which is a separate word.

examples.ko: 시곗바늘이 오후 네 시를 가리키고 있어요.
examples.en: The clock hands are pointing to four in the afternoon.
The clock hands stopped, so I changed the battery.
I can hear the clock hands ticking along.

examples.ko: 아이가 시곗바늘 보는 법을 배우고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is learning how to read the clock hands.
During the exam, I kept staring at the clock hands.
It looks like the clock hands are going backwards.

explain: 짧은 바늘은 '시침', 긴 바늘은 '분침', 가는 바늘은 '초침'이라고 해요. 시곗바늘은 이 바늘들을 모두 부르는 말이에요.
explain_en: The short hand is the '시침', the long hand is the '분침', and the thin hand is the '초침'. 시곗바늘 is the general word for all of them.

examples.ko: 시골길에서 소 한 마리가 천천히 걸어가요.
examples.en: A cow is slowly walking along the country road.

examples.ko: 번잡한 도심을 벗어나 한적한 시골길을 달렸어요.
examples.en: I left the busy city and drove along a quiet country road.
Country roads get really dark at night.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁에 가는 시골길이 아주 좁아요.
examples.en: The country road to my grandmother's house is very narrow.
Cosmos flowers are blooming along the country road.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 시골길은 진흙투성이가 돼요.
examples.en: On rainy days, country roads get covered in mud.

explain: '시골길을 걷다', '시골길을 달리다'처럼 써요. 도시의 길은 보통 '큰길', '골목길'처럼 다르게 불러요.
explain_en: It is used as '시골길을 걷다' (walk along a country road) or '시골길을 달리다' (drive along one). Roads in a city are usually called other things, such as '큰길' (main road) or '골목길' (alley).

examples.ko: 시누이가 주말에 우리 집에 놀러 와요.
examples.en: My husband's sister is coming to visit our house on the weekend.
I get along quite well with my sister-in-law.
I was really grateful to get a gift from my sister-in-law.
My sister-in-law is getting married, so I prepared a gift of money.

examples.ko: 명절에는 시누이 가족이 다 같이 모여요.
examples.en: On holidays, my sister-in-law's family all gathers together.
I went to the market with my sister-in-law.

explain: 남편의 누나와 여동생을 모두 '시누이'라고 해요. 직접 부를 때는 '시누이'라고 하지 않고, 손아래면 '아가씨', 손위면 '형님'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: Both a husband's older sister and younger sister are called 시누이. You don't address her as 시누이 directly; you call a younger one '아가씨' and an older one '형님'.

examples.en: My husband's younger brother is getting married next month.
I work at the same company as my husband's younger brother.
I gave my husband's younger brother a little pocket money.
My husband's younger brother and his wife came to greet us on the holiday.
My husband's younger brother cooks well, so I often eat his food.
My husband's younger brother is three years younger than me.

explain: 남편의 남동생을 가리켜요. 남편의 여동생은 '시누이'예요. 직접 부를 때는 미혼이면 '도련님', 결혼했으면 '서방님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means the husband's younger brother, while the husband's younger sister is a '시누이'. You address him as '도련님' if he is unmarried and '서방님' if he is married.

examples.en: I got so angry that my face turned deep red.

examples.ko: 해가 질 때 하늘이 시뻘겋게 물들었어요.
examples.en: The sky was dyed deep red when the sun set.
The iron on the heater glowed red hot.

examples.ko: 눈이 시뻘건 걸 보니 밤을 새웠나 봐요.
examples.en: Your eyes are bloodshot, so you must have stayed up all night.

examples.ko: 고추장을 너무 많이 넣어서 국물이 시뻘게요.
examples.en: I put in too much gochujang, so the broth is bright red.
Deep red flames shot up into the sky.

explain: '빨갛다'보다 훨씬 진하고 강한 느낌이에요. 선명하고 밝은 빨강은 '새빨갛다'를 써요. ㅎ 불규칙이라 '시뻘게요', '시뻘건'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It feels much deeper and stronger than '빨갛다'. For a vivid, bright red, use '새빨갛다'. It is an irregular ㅎ adjective, so it becomes '시뻘게요' and '시뻘건'.

examples.ko: 부모님이 딸을 시집보내고 나서 많이 우셨어요.
examples.en: My parents cried a lot after marrying off their daughter.
My father felt empty after marrying off his youngest daughter.
They say in the old days, daughters were married off at around eighteen.
The house became quiet after my older sister was married off.

examples.ko: 딸을 시집보내려고 몇 년 동안 돈을 모았어요.
examples.en: I saved money for years to marry off my daughter.
I have no plans yet to marry off my daughter.

explain: 딸이 결혼해서 남편 집으로 가는 것을 부모의 입장에서 말할 때 써요. 아들이 결혼하는 경우에는 '장가보내다'를 써요. 짝이 되는 말은 '시집가다'와 '시집오다'예요.
explain_en: It describes a daughter marrying and going to her husband's family, from the parents' point of view. For a son marrying, use '장가보내다'. Related words are '시집가다' and '시집오다'.

examples.ko: 어머니는 스무 살에 이 마을로 시집오셨어요.
examples.en: My mother came to this village as a bride at twenty.

examples.ko: 외국에서 시집온 며느리가 한국말을 아주 잘해요.
examples.en: The daughter-in-law who married in from abroad speaks Korean very well.
It's my first holiday since marrying into the family, so I'm nervous.

examples.ko: 제가 시집왔을 때는 이 동네가 지금과 많이 달랐어요.
examples.en: When I first came here as a bride, this neighborhood was very different from now.
They say my grandmother came as a bride from a distant village.

examples.ko: 시집오기 전에는 요리를 거의 못 했어요.
examples.en: Before I got married and came here, I could hardly cook.

explain: 여자가 결혼해서 남편 집안의 일원이 되는 것을 시댁 쪽에서 볼 때 써요. 반대로 친정 쪽에서 보면 '시집가다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a woman marries and joins her husband's family, seen from the husband's family side. From her own family's side, you use '시집가다' instead.

examples.ko: 어제 부딪힌 곳에 시퍼렇게 멍이 생겼어요.
examples.en: A dark blue bruise formed where I bumped myself yesterday.

examples.ko: 뛰놀다가 넘어져서 무릎에 시퍼런 멍이 들었어요.
examples.en: I fell while playing and got a deep blue bruise on my knee.
My lips turned blue in the cold weather.
I felt scared looking at the deep blue sea.

examples.ko: 깊은 바다 색이 시퍼레서 들어가기 무서워요.
examples.en: The deep sea is such a dark blue that I'm scared to go in.

examples.ko: 며칠이 지나도 시퍼런 멍이 안 없어져요.
examples.en: Even after several days, the dark blue bruise won't go away.

explain: '퍼렇다'보다 더 짙고 강한 푸른색이에요. 멍, 입술, 바다처럼 진한 색에 자주 써요. ㅎ 불규칙이라 '시퍼레요', '시퍼런'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.example: 내 눈이 시퍼렇게 살아 있는 한 그런 일은 없을 거예요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 멀쩡히 살아 있어서 그런 일을 허락하지 않겠다는 강한 말투예요. 보통 화가 났을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A strong way of saying that as long as you are alive, something will not be allowed. Usually said when angry.

explain_en: It is a darker, stronger blue than '퍼렇다', and is often used for bruises, lips and deep sea. It is an irregular ㅎ adjective, so it becomes '시퍼레요' and '시퍼런'.

examples.ko: 식목일에 가족과 함께 산에서 나무를 심었어요.
examples.en: On Arbor Day, I planted trees in the mountains with my family.
Arbor Day is April 5th every year.

examples.ko: 식목일 행사로 공원에 묘목을 심으러 갔어요.
examples.en: For the Arbor Day event, I went to plant saplings in the park.
Tomorrow is Arbor Day, so I will plant trees with the kids.
Where do you go to plant trees on Arbor Day?

examples.ko: 올해 식목일에는 비가 와서 행사가 미뤄졌어요.
examples.en: It rained this Arbor Day, so the event was postponed.

explain: '식목'은 나무를 심는다는 한자어라 보통 '식목일'로만 나와요. 일상에서 나무를 심는 일은 그냥 '나무를 심다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '식목' is a Sino-Korean word for planting trees and mostly appears only in '식목일'. In everyday speech, planting trees is simply '나무를 심다'.

examples.en: My child left the shoe bag at school.
You have to take your indoor shoes in a shoe bag.
It is dangerous to swing your shoe bag while walking.

examples.ko: 엄마가 아이 신발주머니에 이름을 써 줬어요.
examples.en: Mom wrote the child's name on the shoe bag.
The shoe bag got dirty, so I washed it in the washing machine.

examples.ko: 새 학기에 맞춰 신발주머니를 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a new shoe bag for the new school term.

explain: 학교에서 신는 실내화를 넣어 다니는 작은 주머니를 말할 때 자주 써요. '실내화 주머니'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is often used for the small bag that carries indoor shoes worn at school. It is also called '실내화 주머니'.

examples.en: I bought rice flour to make rice cakes.
Bread made from rice flour is very chewy.
If you mix rice flour into the batter, it gets crispier.

examples.ko: 쌀가루 반죽을 한 시간 동안 두세요.
examples.en: Leave the rice flour dough for an hour.
Can I use rice flour instead of wheat flour?
Store the rice flour in a cool place.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '밀가루'예요. 떡, 전, 빵을 만들 때 쌀가루를 쓰기도 하는데, 밀가루와 반죽 느낌이 달라서 레시피대로 쓰는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '밀가루' (wheat flour). Rice flour is also used for rice cakes, pancakes and bread, but the dough feels different from wheat dough, so it is best to follow the recipe.

examples.ko: 동네 쌀집에서 쌀 한 포대를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a sack of rice at the neighborhood rice shop.

examples.ko: 쌀집 아저씨가 쌀을 집까지 배달해 줬어요.
examples.en: The man from the rice shop delivered the rice to my house.
The number of rice shops has dropped a lot these days.

examples.ko: 쌀집에 가면 잡곡도 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go to a rice shop, you can also buy mixed grains.

examples.ko: 우리 집 앞에는 오래된 쌀집이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is an old rice shop in front of my house.
The rice shop sells freshly milled rice.

explain: '쌀가게'도 같은 곳을 가리켜요. '쌀집 아저씨'처럼 가게 주인을 편하게 부를 때도 써요.
explain_en: '쌀가게' refers to the same kind of place. People also use it casually for the owner, as in '쌀집 아저씨'.

examples.en: I went to eat ssambap near my office.

examples.ko: 쌈밥 정식에는 쌈 채소가 아주 많이 나와요.
examples.en: The ssambap set comes with a lot of leafy vegetables.
With ssambap, you add ssamjang and wrap it up to eat.
At the ssambap restaurant, I ordered doenjang stew as well.

examples.ko: 집에서 상추와 깻잎으로 쌈밥을 싸 먹었어요.
examples.en: At home, I wrapped rice in lettuce and perilla leaves and ate it.
Ssambap without meat is also good because it is healthy.

explain: '쌈'은 채소에 밥이나 반찬을 싸 먹는 것이고, '쌈밥'은 그렇게 밥을 싸 먹는 식사예요. 식당에서는 '쌈밥 정식'이라는 메뉴로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '쌈' means wrapping rice or side dishes in vegetable leaves, and '쌈밥' is a meal eaten that way. At restaurants it often appears on menus as '쌈밥 정식' (ssambap set meal).

examples.ko: 아이들이 말을 안 들어서 속을 썩여요.
examples.en: The kids don't listen, so they cause me a lot of worry.

examples.ko: 제발 엄마 속 좀 그만 썩이세요.
examples.en: Please stop worrying your mom so much.

examples.ko: 부모님 속을 썩인 일이 지금도 마음에 걸려요.
examples.en: I still feel bad about the times I troubled my parents.

examples.ko: 학생 때 선생님 속을 많이 썩였어요.
examples.en: When I was a student, I gave my teachers a lot of trouble.

examples.ko: 자꾸 속을 썩이면 친구들도 떠나갈 거예요.
examples.en: If you keep causing trouble, even your friends will leave.

examples.ko: 우리 강아지는 아직도 말썽을 피워서 속을 썩이는 중이에요.
examples.en: Our puppy is still causing mischief and giving me a hard time.

explain: 거의 '속을 썩이다' 모양으로 쓰고, 말썽이나 걱정거리 때문에 다른 사람을 힘들게 한다는 느낌이에요. 힘든 사람이 주어이면 '속이 썩다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 동생이 자꾸 말썽을 부려서 부모님 속을 썩여요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이 썩는다는 뜻과 관계없이, 누군가를 마음고생하게 만든다는 관용 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An idiom meaning to cause someone mental distress, unrelated to food rotting.

phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정과 마음고생이 너무 커서 속이 상한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Worry and distress are so great that one is sick at heart.

explain_en: It almost always appears as '속을 썩이다' and means causing someone worry or trouble through bad behavior. When the suffering person is the subject, say '속이 썩다' instead.

examples.en: This book is for children, so the print is big.

examples.ko: 아동용 의자를 식당에서 빌릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can borrow a children's chair at the restaurant.

examples.ko: 이 약은 아동용과 어른용이 따로 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine comes in separate versions for children and adults.
Children's toothbrushes have soft bristles.
I went to the store to buy a children's bike.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 아동용이 아니라서 아이와 보기 어려워요.
examples.en: This movie isn't for children, so it is hard to watch with a kid.

explain: '어린이용'과 같은 뜻인데, 상품 표시나 설명에서는 '아동용'이 더 자주 보여요. 짝이 되는 말은 '어른용'이에요.
explain_en: It means the same as '어린이용', but '아동용' is seen more on product labels and descriptions. The opposite is '어른용' (for adults).

examples.en: Today I wore matching black from top to bottom.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 저를 아래위로 쳐다봐서 불편했어요.
examples.en: That person looked me up and down, and it made me uncomfortable.
The child bobs their head up and down happily.
You open and close the window by moving it up and down.

examples.ko: 아래위로 흔들리는 버스 안에서 책을 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a book on a bus that was bouncing up and down.

examples.ko: 아래위가 똑같은 옷을 입으면 쌍둥이 같아요.
examples.en: If you wear the same top and bottom, you look like twins.

explain: '위아래'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요. 옷 이야기에서는 윗옷과 아래옷을 함께 가리킬 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It can be used with the same meaning as '위아래'. When talking about clothes, it often refers to the top and bottom together.

examples.ko: 그는 말할 때 아래턱을 앞으로 내미는 버릇이 있어요.
examples.en: He has a habit of pushing his lower jaw forward when he talks.
I had an X-ray of my lower jaw taken at the dentist.
My lower jaw hurts, so it is hard to eat.

examples.ko: 아래턱을 움직이며 천천히 씹어야 소화가 잘돼요.
examples.en: You digest better if you chew slowly, moving your lower jaw.

examples.ko: 하품을 크게 했더니 아래턱이 빠질 것 같았어요.
examples.en: I yawned so wide that my lower jaw felt like it would pop out.

examples.ko: 아래턱 선이 갸름해서 인상이 날카로워 보여요.
examples.en: The line of his lower jaw is slim, so he looks sharp.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '위턱'이에요. 일상에서는 보통 그냥 '턱'이라고 하고, 치과나 병원에서 위아래를 나눌 때 '아래턱'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '위턱' (upper jaw). In daily life people usually just say '턱', and '아래턱' is used when distinguishing top from bottom, such as at the dentist or hospital.

examples.en: My lower abdomen hurt, so I went to the hospital.
My lower belly has been sticking out lately, so I started exercising.

examples.ko: 아랫배에 힘을 주고 노래를 불러 보세요.
examples.en: Try singing while tightening your lower belly.

examples.ko: 아랫배를 따뜻하게 하면 도움이 될 거예요.
examples.en: Keeping your lower belly warm should help.
I felt better when I rubbed my lower belly with my hand.
My lower belly gets cold, so I often get stomachaches.

explain: 몸이 아플 때 '배가 아파요'보다 위치를 구체적으로 말하고 싶을 때 써요. 노래나 운동에서 '아랫배에 힘을 주다'라는 말을 자주 들어요.
explain_en: Use it when you want to be more specific than '배가 아파요' about where it hurts. In singing and exercise you often hear '아랫배에 힘을 주다' (tighten the lower belly).
